title: Squash boom: 'I want to be an athlete' is rare for Indian kids
content: Indian squash is enjoying a surge of attention, fuelled by Anahat Singh’s historic World Junior title and a growing pool of top-ranked professionals. But India's star squash player Veer Chotrani believes sustained success requires more than courts and funding. India needs stronger coaching, training partners and a professional ecosystem at home, while families must increasingly view sport as a viable career alongside education.

title: Six Wall Street giants back Nvidia as company answers ‘circular financing’ claims
content: Nvidia collaborates with leading investment firms to secure funding for artificial intelligence infrastructure. This partnership aims to amass hundreds of billions of dollars for AI advancements and improve accessibility to Nvidia's high-performance computing resources. By engaging independent financial institutions, the initiative guarantees real demand for AI solutions, paving the way for a novel financing approach in the rapidly evolving AI sector.

title: Bengaluru: Prajwal Revanna found with phone, pen drive in jail; fresh FIR filed
content: Former MP Prajwal Revanna was found with a mobile phone during a prison raid.  A pen drive and charger were also discovered during the extensive search operation.  Another inmate, Prathap Rai, was similarly found possessing a mobile phone.  An inquiry is underway to determine how these devices entered the central prison facility.  Disciplinary action and notices will be issued after a thorough investigation.

title: 2.5-year-old among 2 dead in Mumbai’s Ville Parle building fire
content: In a heartbreaking incident, a fire ignited in two flats situated on the 11th floor of a Vile Parle building, claiming the lives of two people, one of whom was a young child. Six others suffered injuries that necessitated hospitalization. Firefighters worked tirelessly to extinguish the flames, which took several hours. Investigators are now working to determine the cause of the tragic fire.

title: HC denies bail to ex-commission secretary accused of leaking exam paper to son
content: The Chhattisgarh high court denied bail to a retired IAS officer and former CGPSC secretary. He is accused of leaking 2021 state civil services exam papers to his son. The court found material indicating the officer's involvement in the recruitment process leak. This alleged leak compromised the fairness of the entire competitive examination process. The court cited the gravity of allegations and impact on public recruitment sanctity.

title: Accenture CEO Julie Sweet makes an 'August request' to employees
content: Accenture has implemented a new policy allowing employees to carry over their unused vacation days, aiming to bolster business performance as the fiscal year winds down. CEO Julie Sweet has urged employees to maximize their efforts in these critical weeks. However, this adjustment may inadvertently dissuade workers from taking necessary breaks, raising concerns among investors following a decline in new bookings.

title: Mach 5 and beyond: US plans next-gen hypersonic missile with longer range, greater speed
content: The US military is spearheading efforts to develop groundbreaking hypersonic cruise missile technology through DARPA. The goal is to achieve unprecedented advancements in speed, range, and durability for these weapons. While older systems transition to production, innovative designs are under scrutiny. Emphasis is placed on cost-effectiveness and the capacity for mass production to effectively counteract advanced enemy air defense systems.

title: Hoover Dam submerged a town in 1935; Lake Mead is revealing it again
content: The receding waters of Lake Mead have unveiled the eerie remnants of St. Thomas, a ghost town in Nevada. Originally a thriving Mormon settlement founded in 1865, it was swallowed by rising waters after the Hoover Dam was built in 1938. Now, the lakebed displays its foundations, allowing history enthusiasts a rare opportunity to connect with a bygone era of agricultural significance.

title: Yonkers uncovers buried river, creating 14,000 sq ft of aquatic habitat
content: In 2012, Yonkers, New York, completed a project to uncover a section of the Saw Mill River that had been buried beneath a downtown parking lot since the 1920s. The former Larkin Plaza was turned into a three-acre public park. Within six months, the restored river supported 14,000 square feet of new aquatic habitat and several species.

title: Gemini becomes Google’s fastest-growing consumer product ever: Pichai says ‘thanks’
content: In an impressive achievement, Google's Gemini mobile application has crossed the milestone of one billion monthly active users, making it the quickest-growing consumer product in the company's history. Users are embracing voice commands and visual inputs for a variety of daily tasks. Impressively, the app creates over 150 million images each day for small businesses while gaining considerable traction among Apple device users, broadening its user base.

title: How Jason Kelce’s four daughters changed his life beyond football

The former Philadelphia Eagles star says his children often teach him valuable lessons when he believes he is teaching them. Jason and Kylie Kelce focus on teamwork, confidence, family values and keeping their daughters grounded. For Jason, becoming a “girl dad” has created a meaningful chapter beyond football and reshaped his definition of success.

title: How Caitlin Clark turned a childhood memory into a 22,000-book impact

This program aims to distribute 22,000 books to young readers in Iowa and Indiana, focusing on children from pre-K to eighth grade to enhance their reading abilities. Inspired by her own experience with Scholastic flyers, Clark is passionate about making literacy accessible and enriching the education of thousands of children.

title: Russia kills 10 in Ukraine as Zelenskyy accuses Moscow of using N Korean missiles

Ukraine warned Russia is exploiting its air defense interceptor shortages.  Meanwhile, Ukraine struck Russian oil facilities, causing damage and casualties.  The conflict continues with both sides expanding long-range strike capabilities.

title: 2 dead, 2 injured after landslide hits Mumbai’s Kurla; several feared trapped
content: A devastating landslide hit Gaushiya Chawl in Kurla, Mumbai, on Wednesday morning, prompting immediate emergency response efforts. Fire brigade and police teams have arrived at the scene to assist with the rescue operations. There are concerns for the safety of numerous individuals believed to be trapped beneath the rubble. Authorities are eagerly awaiting updates to assess the full scale of the disaster.

title: Kaif 'surprised' by BCCI's struggle to hire medical professionals amid injury crisis
content: India is grappling with a significant player injury crisis, forcing discussions about the effectiveness of the BCCI's Centre of Excellence. Ex-cricketer Mohammad Kaif expressed astonishment at the board's challenges in securing suitable hires. VVS Laxman added that prospective staff appointments encountered last-minute obstacles. Given the BCCI's robust financial resources, this inability to draw in top talent is perplexing, especially with crucial matches on the horizon.

title: North Korea fires second ballistic missile in a week ahead of US-South Korea war drills
content: North Korea launched a ballistic missile towards the sea on Wednesday. This marks Pyongyang's second reported missile test in less than a week. South Korea and Japan condemned the launch as a provocation. Major US-South Korea military exercises are scheduled to begin soon. North Korea continues its weapons testing program amid international concerns.

title: Tech firm director held over 2022 Jharkhand paper leak from Mumbai; deadlock hardens

The allegations prompted the cancellation of the junior engineer examination. Further investigations revealed the agency's participation in the leak scheme, with five others already detained. The arrested director is now under judicial custody after detailed interrogation by authorities.

title: Mark Zuckerberg's $300M yacht booed over rescue call; clarification issued

Help was already en route when the yacht's crew reviewed the assistance request. The yacht, valued at $390 million, was closer to the distressed skiff. Passengers on a nearby cruise ship booed the yacht's perceived inaction.

title: Cristiano Ronaldo marries longtime partner Georgina Rodríguez in private ceremony

The couple held a private civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, on August 11, 2026, and confirmed the news with a joint Instagram post showing their wedding rings. title: 'Process can’t be unending': Supreme Court wants SIR tribunals in Bengal to work faster
content: the process cannot be so slow that the next assembly elections would be due by the time the appeals are decided . nearly 34 lakh appeals pending adjudication before SIR appellate tribunals against deletion of voters’ names in west Bengal . the Supreme Court decided to take stock of their performance and suggested they speed up their work . a petition complained about the slow rate of disposal of appeals by those whose names were deleted from electoral rolls .
